avatar-1.note: Byte-identical to --warn. Recorded as a known exception, not fixed.

avatar-2.note: The exact blue removed as --brand on 2026-09-05, still live in the avatar palette.

display.purpose: Bricolage 700, 1.6rem. The two big figures on the metrics panel and nothing else; there is no page-title face.

subhead.purpose: Bricolage 700, 0.95rem. List section headings and the loan name on a collapsed row; the two agree by design.

title.purpose: Bricolage 600, 0.82rem. The base button and dense header chrome: the display face at body scale.

body.purpose: DM Sans 400, 14px. The document base and full-width form fields.

body-sm.purpose: DM Sans 400, 0.85rem. Prose inside a card: notes, message bubbles, leaderboard names. Most sentences in the app are read at this size, not the 14px base.

control.purpose: DM Sans 600, 0.78rem. Small buttons, field labels, menu items. The busiest step in the stylesheet.

label.purpose: JetBrains Mono 500/600, 0.68rem, 0.06em. Status pills, ratio captions, counts. Non-prose only.

micro-label.purpose: JetBrains Mono 600, ~0.6rem uppercase. The collapsed row's mono chrome; the tier the coarse-pointer touch floor raises to 11px.

shadows.name: resting
shadows.purpose: Deliberate no-op, never the keyword none. Surfaces are flat at rest; depth is the tone step plus a hairline.

shadows.name: lifted
shadows.purpose: The only real shadow. Hover, an expanded row, and anything floating: menus, modals, toasts.

shadows.name: modal
shadows.purpose: A panel that has left the page entirely. Composed on the lifted token, with a 2px border rather than a hairline.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: The :focus-visible ring. Never strip an outline without replacing it.

motion.name: slide-up
motion.purpose: Upward-opening panels: share popover, toast host.

motion.name: pulse-overdue
motion.purpose: Overdue tag pulse. Used sparingly; the red date already says it.

motion.name: pulse-unread
motion.purpose: Halo on the unread-note dot, for a party only.

motion.name: pulse-celebrate
motion.purpose: Green halo after a completion milestone, then settles.

motion.name: hover-lift
motion.purpose: Card hover. No transform, no scale.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The brand fill. One per context. Ink, not a hue.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--brand, #1f1c17); color: var(--on-accent, #fff); border: none; border-radius: 5px; padding: 7px 14px; font-family: 'Bricolage Grotesque', 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 0.82rem; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--brand-hover, #000); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(31, 28, 23, 0.35); }

components.name: Good Button
components.description: The positive move on a task: Claim, Merge Done, Submit. The real primary action in most of the app.
components.css: .ds-btn-good { background: var(--good, #2e7d4f); color: var(--on-accent, #fff); border: none; border-radius: 5px; padding: 6px 10px; font-family: 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 0.78rem; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s; } .ds-btn-good:hover { background: #256942; } .ds-btn-good:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(31, 28, 23, 0.35); }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Secondary and cancel. Outline only, never filled. Opts out of the fill through its tokens, never by declaring background on :hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: var(--brand, #1f1c17); border: 1px solid var(--line, #d5d0c7); border-radius: 5px; padding: 7px 14px; font-family: 'Bricolage Grotesque', 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 0.82rem; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: var(--brand-soft, #e9e6df); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(31, 28, 23, 0.35); }

components.name: Status Tag
components.description: Monospace status pill with a leading dot. One per signal role.
components.css: .ds-tag { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 5px; background: var(--hot-bg, #fef0e0); color: var(--hot, #c25e00); border-radius: 4px; padding: 3px 9px; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.68rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.06em; } .ds-tag-dot { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 999px; background: currentColor; }

components.name: Person Chip
components.description: A person, as initials on one of eight hues hashed off their user id. Held clear of the four signal hues so it never reads as urgency.
components.css: .ds-avatar { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 22px; height: 22px; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--avatar-3, #1f7a6c); color: var(--avatar-ink, #fff); font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.62rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.02em; }

components.name: Task Card
components.description: The raised surface. A hairline all the way round, no coloured stroke on any side: status is carried by the court section the row sits in and by the button the row offers.
components.html:
LOI CHECK
Marbury Ridge — 214 Alder St
components.css: .ds-card { background: var(--panel, #fefdfb); color: var(--ink, #14120f); border: 1px solid var(--line-soft, #e8e4dd); border-radius: 8px; padding: 12px; box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm, 0 0 0 0 transparent); transition: box-shadow 0.15s; } .ds-card:hover { box-shadow: var(--shadow-md, 0 6px 18px -6px rgba(26,24,20,0.22)); } .ds-card-type { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.68rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.06em; color: var(--muted, #6f6a63); } .ds-card-title { font-family: 'Bricolage Grotesque', 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 700; margin-top: 4px; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Panel ground, strong rule, brand focus ring.
components.css: .ds-input { background: var(--panel, #fefdfb); color: var(--ink, #14120f); border: 1px solid var(--line, #d5d0c7); border-radius: 6px; padding: 7px 10px; font-family: 'DM Sans', 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; width: 100%; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--muted, #6f6a63); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: var(--brand, #1f1c17); box-shadow: var(--focus-ring, 0 0 0 2px rgba(31,28,23,0.35)); }

components.name: Section Header
components.description: The only grouping device in the app: a heading, a monospace count chip, and a hairline. The count chip on --bg-soft is the system's one recorded contrast exception at 4.3:1.
components.css: .ds-section-head { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; padding: 10px 0 6px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line, #d5d0c7); } .ds-section-head h2 { margin: 0; font-family: 'Bricolage Grotesque', 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 0.95rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: -0.01em; color: var(--ink, #14120f); } .ds-section-count { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.72rem; color: var(--muted, #6f6a63); background: var(--bg-soft, #eae7e0); padding: 2px 7px; border-radius: 3px; } @media (pointer: coarse) { .ds-section-count { font-size: 11px; } }

components.name: Tab Bar
components.description: Underline-active tabs, no fill. Rendered for admins only.
components.css: .ds-tabs { display: flex; gap: 4px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line-soft, #e8e4dd); } .ds-tab { background: none; border: none; border-bottom: 2px solid transparent; padding: 8px 12px; font-family: 'Bricolage Grotesque', 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 0.82rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--muted, #6f6a63); cursor: pointer; } .ds-tab:hover { color: var(--ink, #14120f); } .ds-tab-active { color: var(--ink, #14120f); border-bottom-color: var(--brand, #1f1c17); }

components.name: Row Quick Action (forward tier)
components.description: Tier one of the collapsed row's action slot: a filled press that MOVES THE WORK FORWARD. Claim, Merge Done, Send Items, Submit, Approve Merge. Fixed 116px track so the action column never goes ragged.
components.css: .ds-quick-action { width: 100%; max-width: 116px; white-space: nowrap; background: var(--good, #2e7d4f); color: var(--on-accent, #fff); border: none; border-radius: 5px; padding: 6px 10px; font-family: 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 0.78rem; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s; } .ds-quick-action:hover { background: #256942; } .ds-quick-action:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(31, 28, 23, 0.35); }

components.name: Row Quick Action (terminal tier)
components.description: Tier two, added 2026-09-06: an outlined press that ENDS THE RECORD. Complete, Confirm, Approve, Archive. Same track and metrics as the filled tier so only the paint changes, and it asks before it fires. There is no third tier.
components.css: .ds-quick-action-terminal { width: 100%; max-width: 116px; white-space: nowrap; background: transparent; color: var(--brand, #1f1c17); border: 1px solid var(--line, #d5d0c7); border-radius: 5px; padding: 6px 10px; font-family: 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 0.78rem; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s; } .ds-quick-action-terminal:hover { background: var(--brand-soft, #e9e6df); } .ds-quick-action-terminal:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(31, 28, 23, 0.35); }

components.name: Terminal Confirm
components.description: The pause in front of a press that cannot be undone from the row. Borrows the two-step Cancel confirm's shape and drops its red ground: red belongs to cancelling, and completing is the work going right.
components.html: Archive this task?
components.css: .ds-terminal-confirm { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 8px 10px; border: 1px solid var(--line, #d5d0c7); border-radius: 6px; background: var(--panel, #fefdfb); color: var(--ink, #14120f); font-family: 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 0.82rem; } .ds-terminal-confirm-q { margin-right: auto; } .ds-terminal-confirm-yes, .ds-terminal-confirm-no { border-radius: 5px; padding: 6px 10px; font-family: 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 0.78rem; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; } .ds-terminal-confirm-yes { background: var(--brand, #1f1c17); color: var(--on-accent, #fff); border: none; } .ds-terminal-confirm-yes:hover { background: var(--brand-hover, #000); } .ds-terminal-confirm-no { background: transparent; color: var(--brand, #1f1c17); border: 1px solid var(--line, #d5d0c7); } .ds-terminal-confirm-no:hover { background: var(--brand-soft, #e9e6df); }

components.name: Waiting Label
components.description: The passive resolution of the action slot when the ball is in someone else's court. Reads 'Unread reply' then 'Read reply' when the message pull is what put the row in Needs you, so the slot never contradicts the heading above it; otherwise 'Waiting on <first name>'. Never a button.
components.css: .ds-waiting-label { display: block; width: 116px; text-align: center; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.6rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted, #6f6a63); } @media (pointer: coarse) { .ds-waiting-label { font-size: 11px; } }

narrative.overview:
This is a bookkeeping pad, not a SaaS dashboard. Off-white paper, ink-black text, sharp typography, and narrow bands of color used strictly as signal. The reference object is a ruled accounting page that someone competent has been annotating all morning: dense, ordered, legible at a glance, with nothing decorative competing for the eye. Every color that is not paper or ink is carrying information.

The system's real subject is a single component, the collapsed task row, and almost every rule here exists to keep that row scannable. It is deliberately saturated: the working assumption is that the row is full, so a new field replaces an existing one rather than joining it. Density is a feature, and the discipline that makes density survivable is that the same fact is always encoded in the same place. Lateness is the number it is about. A person is a colored chip. None of these channels borrow each other's vocabulary, and the edge markers were deleted in one pass because each repeated in the margin what the row already said in words.

The dark theme is a different room, on purpose. It is not the warm ledger with the lights off; it is an indigo ledger, settled after five whole palettes were driven live, including a faithful dark rendering of the light theme, which lost. A third theme, contrast, is pure black and white with no shadows at all and a deliberately monochrome person-chip set.

Rendered size is the only size on a phone. Zoom is disabled in the Teams mobile webview, in three layers and on purpose, so on 2026-09-06 the stylesheet gained a type floor for the text people read, matching the floor it already applied to the text they type into.
keyCharacteristics: Paper-and-ink ground; color appears only where it means something.
Three fully independent themes, not one theme with a filter over it.
A saturated primary row, defended against accretion.
Typography carries the hierarchy that color is not allowed to carry.
Restrained motion: a short list of named animations and nothing else.
Contrast ratios are measured and recorded, not eyeballed.

rules.name: The Role-Not-Hue Rule
rules.body: Signal tokens are named for what they mean, never for what color they are. A theme may answer bad with a rose and good with a mint; code that assumes red and green is wrong, not the theme. The corollary, learned on the metrics panel: a chart that only counts how many of a thing were filed may not borrow a signal token to tell its categories apart, because painting Fraud Check in --bad claims fraud checks are failing. Categories get length, weight or an annotation. One bar, one color.

rules.name: The One Warm Note Rule
rules.body: In the dark theme, the indigo frame carries one warm accent and no more. Every signal but warn is rotated to the cool side of its own hue. A new signal color gets cooled before it lands; the warm slot is taken.

rules.name: The Three-Theme Rule
rules.body: A new themeable color is not done until it exists in all three :root blocks. There is no fallback and no derivation; contrast in particular is authored, not computed.

rules.name: The Measured Floor Rule
rules.body: Body text clears 4.5:1 against its own panel and hairlines clear the 3:1 UI-component minimum, per theme, verified against that theme's panel rather than assumed from the light one. Verify against the tone the text actually sits on, not the panel behind it: the section-count chip is the standing counterexample, passing at 5:1 on --panel and failing at 4.3:1 on --bg-soft.

rules.name: The On-Accent Rule
rules.body: Text and icons on a filled accent read on-accent, never #fff. The light theme's accents are dark enough for white ink; the dark and contrast themes use bright pastel fills where white collapses to roughly 2.8:1.

rules.name: The One Hardcode Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one literal color left in the stylesheet: #256942, the hover fill on the filled green button, with no --good-hover token behind it. It is a known exception, scoped out rather than fixed. Nothing new joins it.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Not-Prose Rule
rules.body: The monospace face is reserved for non-prose: dates, counts, type labels, section counts, status pills. Prose stays in DM Sans. The two never mix inside a sentence.

rules.name: The One Exception That Proves It
rules.body: An LOI's request field is drawn in the fixed-width face, because it holds a pasted term sheet and a term sheet only lines up in one. That is the single prose-shaped box allowed a mono face, and it earns it by being tabular data wearing a paragraph's clothes.

rules.name: The Touch Floor Rule
rules.body: On a coarse pointer, mono chrome floors at 11px and anything read rather than glanced at floors at 12px. Measured at a 390px viewport before the floor landed: due labels at 8.8px, the waiting label at 9.6px, the type label at 10.88px, none different from their 1440px size. The floor block is the last block in styles.css and must stay there.

rules.name: The Saturated Row Rule
rules.body: The collapsed task row is intentionally full. A new field replaces an existing one; it does not join the queue. If nothing can be given up, the field does not belong on the row.

rules.name: The Nothing-Behind-The-Fold Rule
rules.body: The collapsed row carries the primary action and the menu, so no actionable control is hidden by collapse.

rules.name: The Grow-The-Target-Not-The-Box Rule
rules.body: A press target that is too small on a phone gets a transparent ::after overlay, not a bigger box, because the menu trigger's 32px is load-bearing on the action column's alignment. 40px rather than 44px: at 44px the overlay would meet the quick action 6px away and Archive would catch presses meant for the menu.

rules.name: The List Does Not Move Itself Rule
rules.body: The list never re-sorts under a viewer. Opening a task carrying an unread reply marks it seen, which would drop the message pull and relocate the row mid-read, so a pulled task is held in the section it was opened in until it is collapsed again. The hold is deliberately not persisted: it means somebody is reading this right now, and a reload legitimately re-sorts.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: A surface that has not been interacted with and is not floating gets no shadow. If a component needs to look separated while sitting still, it gets a hairline and a tone step, not elevation.

rules.name: The Never-none Rule
rules.body: Both shadow tokens are transparent no-ops, never the keyword none, including in the contrast theme which has no shadows. The celebrating card composes them with a halo shadow, and none inside a box-shadow list voids the entire declaration.

rules.name: The One Definition Rule
rules.body: A measurement two components must agree on is declared once, as a token, and read from there. Every alignment defect in this system has been the same shape: the same number written down twice, and one copy moving.

rules.name: The Breakpoint-Order Rule
rules.body: A media query adds no specificity, so a responsive override placed above the rule it overrides simply loses, silently, forever. Every phone override goes after its base rule. The corollary: a block that raises values across many class-scoped rules must sit below all of them, which is why the touch floors are the last block in the file.

rules.name: The Empty-Bar Rule
rules.body: Nothing goes in the app bar. In production it holds admin-only tabs and nothing else, so a control placed there is a control most people never see.

rules.name: The Two-Tier Action Rule
rules.body: The collapsed row's action slot has two tiers and exactly two. A filled button moves the work forward: Claim, Merge Done, Send Items, Submit, Approve Merge. An outlined one ends the record: Complete, Confirm, Approve, Archive. Same track, same metrics, only the paint changes. This narrows the earlier single-style rule rather than reverting it: the good/ghost/danger split really did read as three inconsistent buttons for one job, and the answer is one rule with two answers, not three styles again. A third tier is not available.

rules.name: The Neutral Confirm Rule
rules.body: A terminal press asks before it fires, in the two-step Cancel confirm's shape with its red ground dropped. Red belongs to cancelling, which is the destructive move; completing and archiving are the work going right, and dressing them in the failure color would tell somebody their finished task went wrong at the moment they finished it.

dos: Do reach for an existing token before defining a color. Every color in the app goes through a custom property on :root, with one recorded exception.
Do add any new themeable value to all three themes, light, dark, and contrast, before considering it done.
Do keep the monospace face for things that are counted or labeled, the body face for anything that reads as a sentence, and the display face for headings and controls.
Do pick a step off the recorded ramp. Nine steps is already more than a dense app needs; a tenth has to displace one.
Do replace a field on the collapsed row rather than appending one.
Do encode every state in at least two channels. Color is never the only signal.
Do make a filled control take its label color from the on-accent token.
Do check a new tint against the panel of the theme it lives in, and against the tone the text actually sits on rather than the one behind it.
Do give a link a standing underline. The light theme's interactive color is ink.
Do separate a block with a hairline, a margin rule, or a tone step. One device, never a container.
Do declare a shared measurement once and read it everywhere.
Do let the label shrink before the box does. On a surface with zoom disabled an overflow is unreachable rather than merely awkward.
Do put a coarse-pointer floor at the bottom of the stylesheet, below every rule it raises, and grow a press target with an overlay rather than a size.
Do ask before a press that cannot be undone from the row, in the neutral confirm shape.
donts: Don't hardcode a hex value anywhere, including white. The green button's hover is the one that got away and is not a precedent.
Don't name anything for its color. The signal tokens are roles.
Don't borrow a signal token to tell categories apart. A chart that counts things has no failing state to report, and a gradient implies a scale the number does not have.
Don't add a warm accent to the dark theme. Cool it first; the one warm slot is spoken for.
Don't add a resting shadow to anything, or write the keyword none into a shadow token.
Don't put a card inside a card.

Don't answer a new state with an edge marker. A colored border or stripe on the side of a card is the most recognizable tell of generated UI, and a fact with a column or a label does not also need a margin.
Don't add a third tier to the row's action slot. Filled moves work forward, outlined ends the record; a new action picks one.
Don't dress a successful ending in the failure color. Red is for cancelling and for failing.
Don't introduce a new animation without checking the existing set first. No scroll effects, no parallax, no transitions on color or text.
Don't let a card move itself, and don't let the list move under a reader.
Don't let the section a row sits in disagree with the button it offers.
Don't treat the dark theme as the light theme dimmed.
Don't put an actionable control behind the collapse.
